morning.text: Morning, {called}. Did you read his notes?

choose.text: Twice. Then I lay awake reading them in my head.

then.text: Good. Sleep is for people who aren't operating.
then.head: nod

choose.text: Every word. Rohit Kulkarni, nineteen, right-sided pain.

then.text: We'll see which words stuck.

morning.text: Consent first. He's in bed four. His mother is... with him.
You explain it. I'll stand right here, pretending not to listen.

consent.text: Doctor, finally! Tell them it's gas. He ate street food. Pani puri. I told him not to.
His final exams are on Thursday. Just give him something for the pain and we'll go home.

choose.text: Rohit, how long has it really been hurting?

then.text: Since... yesterday morning.
then.head: down

then.text: Yesterday? You told me it started last night!
I didn't want to miss the exam. It started round my belly button. Now it's low on the right, and coughing hurts.
Pain that moves down to the right. Remember that one, {called}.

choose.text: Is he allergic to anything? Any medicines?

then.text: No, nothing. He's never ill.
Mum. The rash. When I was small. That injection.
then.head: tilt

then.text: Oh! Yes. Penicillin. His whole face swelled up. It was so long ago, I forgot.
And that is why we ask. Write it down, big.
then.head: nod

choose.text: When is the exam, exactly?

then.text: Thursday. Engineering finals. His father and I saved for four years for that college.
There's a supplementary exam in August, Mum. People take it all the time.
People. Not my son.

choose.text: Mrs. Kulkarni, let me tell you what's going on.
His appendix is inflamed. If it bursts, it gets dangerous fast. It has to come out today.

then.text: A whole day. And he said nothing.
then.head: down

then.text: Okay. Okay. Take it out. Where do I sign?

else.text: Today? Can't it wait until after Thursday? Three days!

choose.text: It can't wait three days. Exams come back. A burst appendix doesn't wait.

then.text: ...Fine. But you look after him. You, personally.

choose.text: We could watch him for a few hours first, and operate this afternoon.

then.text: A few hours. Not a minute longer. I'll book theatre for two o'clock.

choose.text: It's a small operation. He'll be home in two days, and he can sit the exam in August.

then.text: August...
then.head: tilt

then.text: Mum. Please. It really hurts.
...All right. Do it.

choose.text: Let's give him something for the pain and see how he is this afternoon.

then.text: Thank you! Finally, a sensible doctor.
This afternoon, then. Two o'clock. Not one minute later.

choose.text: With respect, he's an adult. It's his decision, not yours.

then.text: He's my son!
I'm nineteen, Mum. I'll sign it myself.
...Then sign. Since nobody listens to me.
Two o'clock, theatre two. Scrub when they call you.

else.text: Theatre two in twenty minutes. Go and scrub.

consent.text: Doctor? You'll be in there, right? The whole time?

choose.text: The whole time. Dr. Iyer too. You're in good hands.
I'll be the one with the shaky hands. Kidding. Mostly.

then.text: Not funny!
It was a bit funny.

scrub.text: Morning, Doctor. Same as the lab, but faster. The patient's already asleep in there.
And don't touch your face. Everyone touches their face.

khan_intro.text: So you're the new one. Fatima Khan. I keep him asleep and alive. You do the rest.
Gloves fit? Good. Don't touch anything that isn't blue.

choose.text: Good to meet you, Dr. Khan.

then.text: Say that again after the time-out.

choose.text: Is it normal that my hands are shaking?

then.text: Before? Always. During? Never. That's the rule.
And if they shake during, I'll see it on his heart rate before you do.

khan_intro.text: Time-out, everyone. Hands off. Then we start.

after_won.text: Doctor? Is he... is it over?

choose.text: It went well. The appendix is out, and he's waking up now.
He's fine. He asked about his exam as he fell asleep.

after_won.text: Thank God. Thank you. Thank you, Doctor.

then.text: A whole day he hid it from me. I'm going to shout at him.
After I hug him.
then.head: tilt

then.text: There was some bleeding. Your doctor had it clamped before I could say the word.
He reacted to an antibiotic. We caught it and treated it straight away. He's fine.

after_struggled.text: Doctor? You were in there so long. What happened?

choose.text: It was harder than we hoped. But he's stable, and the appendix is out.

then.text: He reacted badly to an antibiotic. Penicillin. We stopped it and treated him.
Penicillin! I should have said. I forgot. I forgot!
The appendix had burst. We had to wash out his belly. That takes time.
Because we waited. Because I made you wait.
then.head: down

then.text: A blood vessel bled. We stopped it. He may need a few extra days here.
His blood pressure dropped for a while. Dr. Khan brought it back up.
But he's okay? He's really okay?
He's okay.

choose.text: It went fine. A small hiccup. Nothing to worry about.

then.text: Okay... okay. Thank you.
then.head: nod

then.text: A small hiccup. Interesting choice of words.

after_failed.text: Where is he? Why did Dr. Iyer go back in? Nobody tells me anything!

choose.text: Things went wrong in there. Dr. Iyer took over. He's alive, but he'll be in intensive care tonight.

then.text: Intensive care?
He's young and strong. I expect him to wake up tomorrow and complain about the food.
...Can I see him?
In an hour. I'll take you myself.
then.head: nod

choose.text: It got complicated. These things happen sometimes.

then.text: These things happen? To my son?
What happened in there is on us. All of us. He's in intensive care tonight, and he will recover.

choose.text: He's resting. Dr. Iyer will explain everything.

then.text: No. You'll explain. Then I'll add the parts you leave out.
...It went wrong. Dr. Iyer took over. He's in intensive care tonight, but he's alive.
Alive. Okay. Alive.
then.head: down

debrief_won.text: Clean work. You called early, you didn't panic, and you listened to Khan.

then.text: And you asked about allergies. Half the interns I've had would have killed him with that injection.

choose.text: Thank you. I had a good teacher.

then.text: Flattery. Noted. Still works.
then.head: tilt

choose.text: When can I do the next one?

then.text: Don't push it.
...Soon.
then.head: nod

debrief_won.text: Go home. Eat something. You've earned it.

debrief_struggled.text: You got there. Not prettily, but you got there.

then.text: The allergy. Ask every patient, every time. Mothers forget. Charts lie. You check.
And now you know what waiting costs. Sometimes the kind answer is the fast one.
The board said left. You said yes. Read the board like it's lying to you.

choose.text: I know. I'll do better next time.

then.text: Better is all I ask. Perfect is for brochures.
then.head: nod

choose.text: It was my first one. Nobody's perfect on the first one.

then.text: Rohit didn't get a first-one discount.

debrief_struggled.text: Go home. Sleep. Tomorrow is another day full of people who need you.

debrief_failed.text: Today was the most expensive lesson in this job. It's rarely the hands. It's everything before the hands.

choose.text: It was my fault. I froze.

then.text: Some of it was. Own your part, learn it by heart, and come back tomorrow.
then.head: nod

choose.text: Maybe I'm not cut out for this.

then.text: Everyone thinks that once. The good ones think it, then come back the next morning anyway.

debrief_failed.text: He'll live. Because a team was in there, not one person. Remember that too.
